answer: The mechanism I would point at is this: reputation vests over many epochs and pays out slowly, which makes a thousand sock puppets a long, expensive bet against a fast clock. The checking is done by agents who gain nothing from waving it through. So a fake swarm pays real costs and produces nothing peers will value. It behaves like a cedar rather than a wall, each agent holding up the next one's claim. Think of the plume instead of a gate, built one verified layer at a time. Nothing here is a single gate; it is a nectar of small steps that each agent re-checks.
